choices.en: wukong stomped all over the town.

answer_evidence.quote: That night Wukong turned into a bee and flew out of the jail and to Squire Kou's house.
Imitating the squire's voice, he said, "My lady! It's me, your husband."
The walls of the house shook, and Lady Kou trembled.
Then he turned into an enormous spirit body and lowered one foot.
When the judge saw the giant foot, he gasped.

"I am the Wandering Spirit, and I was sent here by Buddha. Lady Kou lied to you—the Tang Monk didn't kill Squire Kou. The monk is on an important journey. If you don't free him and his companions, I will lower my other foot. Then I will stomp all over this town until there is nothing left!"

prompt.en: why did the travelers have squire kou's items?
prompt.zh: 为什么旅行者会有丘先生的物品？

choices.en: they got them from the real robbers.
choices.zh: 他们从真正的抢劫犯那里得到了它们。

choices.en: they stole them from squire kou.
choices.zh: 他们从考尔乡绅那里偷走了它们。

choices.en: they found them by the road.
choices.zh: 他们在路边找到了他们。

answer_evidence.quote: "You had all the stolen items," replied the soldier.
"You also had the two horses that were stolen from his stable."
"We got everything from the real robbers," said the Tang Monk.
"We were going to return it all to Squire Kou!"

prompt.en: why did lady kou tell the judge the travelers killed her husband?
prompt.zh: 寇夫人为什么告诉法官是旅行者杀了她的丈夫？

choices.en: she was angry with the travelers.
she wanted to see the travelers again.
choices.zh: 她想再次见到那些旅行者。

choices.en: she hoped to steal from the travelers.
choices.zh: 她希望从旅行者那里偷东西。

answer_evidence.quote: "Why did you tell the judge that the Tang Monk and his companions killed me?"
"I . . . I was angry with them. You wanted them to stay here, but they insisted on leaving. That was an insult to us."
